actions.name: drive forward at 30 % without a distance

control_flow: avoidWalls: if RLIGHT < 60, check the FRONT and LEFT obstacles; otherwise call driveInTheDark.
Inside RLIGHT < 60: a FRONT obstacle turns left 15°; else a LEFT obstacle turns right 15°; else call driveInTheDark.
driveInTheDark: if LLIGHT < 70 drive forward at 30 % without waiting; else call stopAtWall.
stopAtWall: if a FRONT obstacle is there stop; else call followLine.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black curve left; else curve right.

likely_intent.description: Drive through a tunnel without hitting its walls, turning away from a wall on the left or ahead.

branches.outcome: the right light is below 60: it checks the obstacle sensors
the right light is 60 or more: it calls driveInTheDark

decision_points.condition: inside dim right light: first a FRONT obstacle, then a LEFT obstacle

branches.outcome: a FRONT obstacle: it turns left 15°
no FRONT obstacle, a LEFT obstacle: it turns right 15°
the left light is below 70: it drives forward at 30 %
the left light is 70 or more: it calls stopAtWall
no FRONT obstacle: it calls followLine

uncertainties: You only mention tunnel walls; the line following and stopping at a wall in bright light are taken from the program.
In a straight tunnel the walls run along the robot, so its forward-looking obstacle sensors do not see them; only a bend or a wall across the tunnel shows a wall.
At a tunnel opening the right light may already be bright while the left light is still dim, so the program may pass the wall check.
